item.title: Rational decomposition of polyhedra and a conjecture of Brlek and Reutenauer
item.description: arXiv:2610.22663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove in the affirmative a conjecture of Brlek and Reutenauer (2003), which relates unambiguous rational sets to a well known result due to Khovanskii and Pukhlikov (1992) and independently to Lawrence (1990) on the valuations of the algebra spanned by the indicator functions of polyhedra.
item.dc:creator: Flavio D'Alessandro, Paolo Papi

item.title: Counting and Sampling Manufacturable Stacking Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.23146v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Designing the stacking sequence of a composite laminate is a discrete optimisation problem: each ply takes one of a few orientations, each evaluation may cost a finite-element solve, and the design must obey manufacturing rules and design guidelines, which optimisers enforce by penalty, repair or rejection. We describe the admissible set exactly. The two manufacturing rules forbid a finite set of factors, so the sequences they admit form a regular language, recognised by an automaton that tracks the last orientation and the length of its run; balance and the ten per cent rule constrain the Parikh vector and are carried by a dynamic program over automaton state and counters. One table, polynomial in N, counts the admissible sequences without producing them, draws them uniformly, and tells whether a partial sequence can still be completed. We give pseudocode, exact counts for three orientation sets, closed-form ceilings on the composition, and four of the five single-rule entries a published table left uncomputed. At 48 plies, 99.8% of the nodes of a layer-wise search tree checking the rules locally have no admissible completion on eight orientations; the completion test removes them. A one-point crossover that cuts two admissible parents only where they share an automaton state and their child closes the counters returns admissible children by construction.
item.dc:creator: Alessio Langiu, Felice Rubino, Giacomo Canale

item.title: The Strong Total Cover Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.23312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Strong Total Cover Problem (STCP) is a novel covering problem defined on a graph $G = (V, E)$, where the objective is to find a minimum-cardinality subset $T \subseteq V \cup E$ such that every element of $V \cup E$ is covered. In this setting, a vertex covers itself and all its incident edges, while an edge covers itself together with its two endpoints. The STCP resembles classical covering problems such as Vertex Cover and Edge Cover problems, and naturally arises as the dual of the total matching problem. In this paper, we investigate the STCP from algorithmic, complexity, and polyhedral perspectives. We first establish close connections between STCP, the Dominating Set Problem, and the Maximum Induced Matching Problem. These relationships provide structural insights, imply the NP-hardness of STCP, and identify graph classes for which the problem is polynomial-time solvable. We then investigate the weighted version of STCP, showing that it remains NP-hard even on complete graphs with binary weights. On the other hand, we present a 2-approximation algorithm, and a polynomial-time algorithm for complete bipartite graphs. On the polyhedral side, we introduce the Strong Total Cover Polytope and derive several families of valid inequalities, some of which are shown to define facets. Finally, we provide a complete linear description of the associated polytope for triangular cactus graphs, revealing an interesting contrast with the considerably more intricate facial structure of the dominating set polytope on cactus graphs.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Aprile, Luca Ferrarini

item.title: From Border-Agnosticism to Causal Rewrite Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.23351v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Causal Graph Rewriting was recently introduced as an evolution of Causal Graph Dynamics to allow for a controlled form of asynchronism in these dynamical systems with dynamical graphs. In this context, the notion of borders---akin to dangling edges---has gained increasing importance. In this paper, we re-examine these borders, interpreting them as missing information. This perspective adds structural rigor to the framework, allowing border-agnostic causal graph rewriting to be reformulated as a rewriting system rather than a dynamical system. This shift represents a crucial step toward facilitating the treatment of reversibility.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Arrighi, Marin Costes, Luidnel Maignan

item.title: Asymptotic dimension of graphs excluding an induced or fat minor
item.description: arXiv:2610.22495v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Asymptotic dimension is a large-scale invariant of metric spaces that was introduced by Gromov (1993). A major open problem in coarse graph theory asks whether, for every fixed graph $H$, the class of graphs excluding $H$ as a fat minor has bounded asymptotic dimension. A weaker conjecture asserts the same conclusion for graphs excluding $H$ as an induced minor. We substantially expand the range of graphs $H$ for which these conjectures are known to hold. Specifically, we prove bounded asymptotic dimension for the following classes of graphs: graphs excluding a fixed planar graph as a fat minor; and graphs excluding a fixed string graph as an induced minor. All of our results also hold for the stronger notion of Assouad--Nagata dimension, a refinement of asymptotic dimension. These results have a number of applications, two of which we mention here. First they imply that an induced minor-closed class is $\chi$-bounded if and only if it does not contain some Burling graph. Second they imply that, in graph classes excluding a fixed planar graph as an induced minor, treewidth is polynomial in maximum degree.
item.dc:creator: Robert Hickingbotham, Freddie Illingworth, Piotr Micek, Bartosz Walczak

item.title: An improved randomized algorithm for finding sinks of Acyclic Unique Sink Orientations of the binary hypercube
item.description: arXiv:2610.22546v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Acyclic Unique Sink Orientations (AUSOs) of the binary hypercube form an elegant abstraction of various optimization problems, ranging from linear programs whose feasibility region is a combinatorial hypercube, to 2-player turn-based stochastic games (2TBSGs) in which one of the players has two actions from each one of its states. The currently fastest known randomized algorithm for finding the sink of such AUSOs is the Random-Facet algorithm of Kalai (STOC 1992), and of Matou\v{s}ek, Sharir and Welzl (SoCG 1992), adapted to the binary hypercube by G\"{a}rtner (RSA 2002). The expected number of vertex queries made by the algorithm is at most $e^{2\sqrt{n}}$, where $n$ is the dimension of the cube. We design an improved randomized sink-finding algorithm that performs an expected number of only $e^{\sqrt{(2+o(1))n}}$ queries. This is the first improved bound for the problem in over two decades. The improved algorithm is obtained by adapting improved versions of the Random-Facet algorithm for solving general linear programs, and LP-type problems, developed by Kalai (STOC 1992), G\"{a}rtner (FOCS 1992), and by Hansen and Zwick (STOC 2015). The improved bound is not implied by these much more general algorithms. A key feature of the improved algorithm and its analysis is its simplicity. The structure of binary AUSOs enables a simpler description and a much simpler analysis of the adapted algorithm. In particular, the recurrence relations bounding the complexity of the algorithm depend on only one variable, and not two, and they can be solved using fairly straightforward techniques.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Dueholm Hansen, Uri Zwick

item.title: Counterexamples to the local antimagic leaf conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.22783v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It has been conjectured that $\chi_{\mathrm{la}}(T)\leq\ell(T)+2$ for every tree $T$ of order at least three, where $\chi_{\mathrm{la}}(T)$ is the local antimagic chromatic number and $\ell(T)$ denotes the number of leaves. We disprove this bound and show that no absolute constant can replace $2$ in an inequality of this form. Our approach uses degree-based intervals containing all possible induced vertex weights under bijective edge labelings, together with a separation criterion that forces selected internal vertex weights to be distinct. We first construct caterpillars $T_3$ and $T_4$ satisfying $\chi_{\mathrm{la}}(T_3)=\ell(T_3)+3$ and $\chi_{\mathrm{la}}(T_4)=\ell(T_4)+4$, respectively. We then construct, for every positive integer $r$, infinitely many pairwise nonisomorphic caterpillars with exactly $r$ internal vertices for which every bijective edge labeling is antimagic. Each such caterpillar $T$ satisfies $\chi_{\mathrm{la}}(T)=|V(T)|=\ell(T)+r$. Consequently, $\chi_{\mathrm{la}}(T)-\ell(T)$ is unbounded even within the class of caterpillars, and no absolute constant $C$ can satisfy $\chi_{\mathrm{la}}(T)\leq\ell(T)+C$ for every tree $T$.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'e Ebling Brondani, Francisca Andrea Macedo Fran\c{c}a

item.title: An Erd\H{o}s-P\'osa theorem for induced packings of even cycles
item.description: arXiv:2610.22967v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that for every graph $G$ and every positive integer $k$, $G$ contains either $k$ vertex-disjoint even cycles with no edges between distinct cycles, or a set of $O(k^2\log k)$ vertices whose closed neighborhood meets every even cycle of $G$. Moreover, we give a polynomial-time algorithm that outputs one of the two outcomes. As an application, we show that every $K_{1,t}$-free graph containing no induced packing of $k$ even cycles has tree-independence number $O(tk^2\log k)$, with a corresponding decomposition computable in polynomial time.
item.dc:creator: Jungho Ahn, Lars Jaffke, O-joung Kwon, Paloma T. de Lima, Hyemi Park

item.title: Complexity of liveness in ring Petri nets and of halting in chip-firing on simple digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.23523v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A ring Petri net (weighted circuit, cyclic weighted T-system) consists of a single directed circuit with arbitrary positive arc weights. We show that deciding liveness of ring Petri nets is coNP-complete, and that coNP-hardness holds in the strong sense already for token-conserving rings, in which every transition consumes and produces the same number of tokens. The proof is a short reduction from the covering problem for systems of residue classes (the complement of Simultaneous Incongruences). Together with a known reduction to circuits, it follows that liveness of weighted T-systems (weighted marked graphs, synchronous dataflow graphs) is coNP-complete, and coNP-hard in the strong sense. As a further consequence, the halting problem for chip-firing on simple directed graphs is NP-complete, which answers a question of Farrell and Levine. On 7 October 2026, the problem of liveness was posed to the AI model Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), which found the reduction, also suggesting the application to the chip-firing problem, and wrote a first version of this paper; the human authors checked it and, together with the model, revised it iteratively into the present form.
item.dc:creator: Eike Best, Raymond Devillers, Petr Jan\v{c}ar, Mat\v{e}j O\v{s}\v{t}\'{a}dal

item.title: Revisiting separators in string graphs, region intersection graphs, and induced-minor-free graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.23792v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: String graphs are intersection graphs of continuous curves in the plane. In 2010, Fox and Pach proved that string graphs with $m$ edges admit balanced vertex separators of size $\mathcal{O}(m^{3/4}\sqrt{\log m})$ and conjectured that this bound can be improved to $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m})$, which would be optimal. After partial progress, Lee claimed in 2017 to prove this conjecture, and more generally to prove analogous separator theorems for region intersection graphs over minor-closed graph families. A key intermediate step in Lee's approach was a padded decomposition scheme for region intersection graphs. In 2024, Korhonen and Lokshtanov extended Lee's approach to the broader setting of graph classes excluding a fixed graph as an induced minor. These results have since found applications in a wide range of works. Later in 2024, a flaw was discovered in the construction of Lee's padded decomposition scheme, invalidating Lee's as well as Korhonen and Lokshtanov's separator results, and many works relying on them. In this work, we prove that string graphs with $m$ edges admit balanced separators of size $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m})$, and more generally obtain analogous $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m})$ bounds for region intersection graphs over fixed minor-closed graph families and for graphs excluding a fixed graph as an induced minor, thereby repairing the vast majority of the affected works. Furthermore, our balanced separators can be found in polynomial time. Our proof uses a different approach from Lee's and does not rely on padded decompositions. Since padded decompositions have also found applications independent of the separator theorems, particularly for string graphs, we also prove a padded decomposition result for region intersection graphs that is optimal for string graphs. We have formalized both the balanced separator and the padded decomposition results in Lean 4 with mathlib.
item.dc:creator: James Davies, Pawe{\l} Rz\k{a}\.zewski, Jack Spalding-Jamieson, Bartosz Walczak

item.title: Online Graph Coloring with Random Arrivals
item.description: arXiv:2610.23824v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study online graph coloring in the random-arrival model, where the vertices are presented in a uniformly random order. Assuming $n$ and $k$ are known in advance, we present a randomized exponential-time algorithm that colors any $k$-colorable graph on $n$ vertices with $O(k^3 \log^2 k \log^4 n)$ colors in expectation. This is the first online coloring algorithm that uses a polylogarithmic number of colors for all fixed $k \geq 3$, and is better than a known lower bound of $\Omega(\log^{k-1} n)$ colors under adversarial arrivals for all fixed $k \geq 6$. In addition, assuming $n$ is known in advance, we obtain a competitive ratio of $\widetilde{O}(n^{2/3})$. For comparison, it is known to be NP-hard to approximate (offline) graph coloring within a factor of $n^{1-\varepsilon}$ for all fixed $\varepsilon > 0$. Therefore, our exponential-time online algorithm achieves a performance guarantee beyond the NP-hardness threshold for polynomial-time approximation algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Hirotaka Yoneda, Masataka Yoneda

item.title: Bounds on the Complete Forcing Numbers of Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2409.17306v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A complete forcing set of a graph is a subset $S$ of its edges with the following property. For any perfect matching $M$, $M$ is the unique perfect matching containing the intersection of $M$ and $S$. The size of a smallest complete forcing set of a graph is called its complete forcing number. In this paper, we propose a polynomial-time algorithm that takes a graph and an ordering of its vertices as input, and outputs a complete forcing set. We analyze the size of the output for a carefully chosen ordering to derive an upper bound on the complete forcing numbers of graphs in terms of other graph-theoretical parameters, such as the degeneracy and the spectral radius of the underlying graph. We compare our results with previous findings in the field. For the class of edge-transitive graphs, we provide an explicit lower bound on the complete forcing number. This result is applied in particular to hypercube graphs and Cartesian powers of even cycles.
item.dc:creator: Javad B. Ebrahimi, Aref Namayandeh, Elahe Tohidi

item.title: Well-quasi-orders on embedded planar graphs
item.description: arXiv:2512.04074v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The central theorem of topological graph theory states that the graph minor relation is a well-quasi-order on graphs. It has far-reaching consequences, in particular in the study of graph structures and the design of (parameterized) algorithms. In this article, we study two embedded versions of classical minor relations from structural graph theory and prove that they are also well-quasi-orders on general or restricted classes of embedded planar graphs. These embedded minor relations appear naturally for intrinsically embedded objects, such as knot diagrams and surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Handling the extra topological constraints of the embeddings requires careful analysis and extensions of classical methods for the more constrained embedded minor relations. We prove that the embedded version of immersion induces a well-quasi-order on bounded carving-width plane graphs by exhibiting particularly well-structured tree-decompositions and leveraging a classical argument on well-quasi-orders on forests. We deduce that the embedded graph minor relation defines a well-quasi-order on plane graphs via their directed medial graphs, when their branch-width is bounded. We conclude that the embedded graph minor relation is a well-quasi-order on all plane graphs, using classical grids theorems in the unbounded branch-width case.
item.dc:creator: Corentin Lunel, Cl\'ement Maria

item.title: An $\widetilde{O}(n^3)$-time FPRAS for the Permanent
item.description: arXiv:2609.20717v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give an FPRAS for the permanent of an $n\times n$ $0/1$ matrix with running time $\widetilde O(n^3)$. Our algorithm extends to a strongly polynomial FPRAS for arbitrary nonnegative matrices with the same running-time bound (but in the unit-cost arithmetic model). Jerrum, Sinclair, and Vigoda (2004) gave the first FPRAS for the permanent of a nonnegative matrix. The running time was subsequently improved to $\widetilde{O}(n^7)$ by Bez\'akov\'a, \v{S}tefankovi\v{c}, Vazirani, and Vigoda (2008), and recently to $\widetilde{O}(n^6)$ by Chen, Vigoda, and Yang (2026). We introduce a multicommodity-flow bound inspired by electrical flows, replacing the usual path-length factor by routing energy. For the classical JSV chain with perfect-matching weights multiplied by $n^2$, we prove a relaxation-time bound of $O(n^3\log n)$ and obtain comparable bounds for estimating the stationary probabilities of having a specified pair of unmatched vertices. We use a separate chain on assignments to generate a warm start at any given temperature, avoiding the long initialization of the JSV chain. Finally, we replace the JSV chain with a new chain that uses only $n$ hole weights and speeds up hole-weight learning by a factor of $n$.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoyu Chen, Heng Guo, Eric Vigoda, Xiongxin Yang

item.title: Tweaking the constant in the Linear Hadwiger Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.10831v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Norin and Steiner recently proved the Linear Hadwiger Conjecture. That is, there is an absolute constant $C$ such that every graph $G$ satisfies $\chi(G)\leqslant C\,\text{had}(G)$, where $\chi(G)$ is the chromatic number and $\text{had}(G)$ is the Hadwiger number of $G$. They estimate that their proof gives a non-optimised constant $C$ of order $10^{100}$. This paper uses AI assistance to optimise their argument, and shows that every graph $G$ satisfies $\chi(G)\,\leqslant\,1{,}118{,}430\,\text{had}(G)$.
item.dc:creator: David R. Wood

item.title: Metric Dimension is NP-complete on Graphs of Treewidth Two
item.description: arXiv:2610.21133v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The metric dimension of a connected graph is the least number of vertices whose distance vectors distinguish all vertices. We show that deciding whether the metric dimension of a graph is at most a given integer is NP-complete on graphs of treewidth at most two. As the problem is polynomial on trees, the graphs of treewidth one, this settles the treewidth threshold of its hardness, which was known to lie between two and twenty-four. The reduction is from satisfiability of formulas in which every literal occurs at most twice. To such a formula with $n$ clauses and $r$ variables it associates a graph $G_\varphi$ of treewidth at most two with $O((n+r)^2)$ vertices, whose metric dimension is $2(n+r)+5$ if the formula is satisfiable and $2(n+r)+6$ otherwise.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Benoit
